lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.focus: definitions of rotation, reflection, and translation
lessonRef.title: Discussion or problem seminar: definitions of rotation, reflection, and translation

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: One approach is shown. There is at least one other that works.

items.prompt: How many rotations under 360° carry a square onto itself?

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: For each, name a second method before you solve it.

items.prompt: Triangle ABC has vertices A(3, -1) and B(-1, -3). After a transformation the images are A′(-3, 1) and B′(1, 3), and the triangle keeps its size and orientation sense. Which single rigid motion describes this?
Point P(-11, 1) is translated by the rule (x, y) → (x + 11, y − 12). Give the image P′.
Reflect the point (10, -2) across the line y = x. Give the image.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: Rotate the point (4, 6) counterclockwise about the origin by 180°. Give the image.
A regular polygon has 12 sides. How many rotations about its centre, strictly between 0° and 360°, carry it onto itself, and what is the smallest such angle?

Triangle ABC has vertices A(-7, -5) and B(-5, 7). After a transformation the images are A′(7, 5) and B′(5, -7), and the triangle keeps its size and orientation sense. Which single rigid motion describes this?

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Argue for one method over another. Say what makes it better, not just that it is.

items.prompt: Point P(-2, -7) is translated by the rule (x, y) → (x + 11, y − 5). Give the image P′.
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: Reflect the point (5, 9) across the x-axis. Give the image.
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
